# Plan — Patch flagged dependency and base-image CVEs in storefront, orders, worker

## Approach

Treat each advisory as its own fix, landed independently per repo, because
the four findings share no code path: `path-to-regexp` and the Alpine base

is in a different artifact. Orders additionally needs a release + chart

# Plan — Patch flagged CVEs in storefront, orders, and worker

## Approach

Fix each of the four scanner findings at its narrowest point — a dependency
version bump or a base-image package upgrade — rather than batching them
into a single cross-repo change. The main alternative considered was one
combined PR/branch touching all three repos at once; that was rejected
because the repos release independently (storefront via its own CI/image
build, orders via `make release` + Helm, worker with no discovered release
pipeline at all), so bundling them would make a single repo's CI failure
block the other two for no reason. The worker finding is treated specially:
the checked-out `uv.lock` already resolves `requests` to a version above the
scan's own fixed-version bar, so the first worker task is a reconciliation
spike, not a code change, to avoid shipping a no-op "fix" or missing the
real, differently-located artifact the scanner actually saw.

## Milestones

### M1 — Worker finding reconciled
Exit criteria:
- [ ] T01 records, with evidence, whether the scanned worker artifact matches this repo's `main`/`uv.lock`
- [ ] If they don't match, T01 names where the real deployed artifact is defined (or states plainly that it could not be found)

### M2 — Fixes merged, CI green
Exit criteria:
- [ ] storefront: `express` bumped so `path-to-regexp` resolves to ≥0.1.12; `npm test`/`npm run lint` pass
- [ ] storefront: Dockerfile change lands `libssl3` ≥3.3.3-r0 in the built image
- [ ] orders: `golang.org/x/net` bumped to ≥0.36.0 in `go.mod`/`go.sum`; `make test`/`make lint` pass
- [ ] worker: `requests` confirmed ≥2.32.4 in whatever artifact is actually deployed — either already true (T01 evidence) or bumped and `uv run pytest` passes

### M3 — Fixed artifacts deployed to production
Exit criteria:
- [ ] storefront image rebuilt (carries both the `express` and `libssl3` fixes) and deployed
- [ ] orders released (`make release`) and rolled out via `helm upgrade --install orders deploy/chart --namespace orders`
- [ ] worker's real deployment (if one exists outside this repo) updated, or explicitly confirmed nothing further is needed

### M4 — Closure confirmed
Exit criteria:
- [ ] All four findings re-verified closed (rescan, or manual version check against the live artifact when a rescan isn't available this sprint)
- [ ] Guardrail metrics (CI pass rate, post-deploy error rate) checked and show no regression

# Plan — Patch flagged CVEs in storefront, orders, and worker

## Approach

Patch each flagged dependency/image independently, repo by repo, since the three services are independently owned and deployed and the four findings span unrelated ecosystems (npm, Go, PyPI, Alpine) with no shared code path. Ship the orders fix through its existing `make release` + Helm chart `image.tag` flow, since orders is the only one of the three with a registered release pipeline; storefront and worker ship through whatever CI/CD they already use for ordinary commits. Close by verifying all four findings against their fixed versions, and against a rescan if the team has access to one.

The main alternative considered was a single combined "upgrade everything" change spanning all three repos in one PR. Rejected: bundling unrelated ecosystems and unrelated review owners into one change raises review and rollback risk for no benefit — if one fix needs rework (e.g. storefront's npm override misbehaving), it would block or revert the other two for no reason.

## Problem statement (required)

The security team's scan flagged four known CVEs across three production
services: an outdated `path-to-regexp` in storefront, an outdated
`golang.org/x/net` in orders, an outdated `requests` in worker, and a
vulnerable `libssl3` package in the Alpine base image storefront ships on.
Each has a fixed version already published. Until patched, these services
carry known, publicly-tracked vulnerabilities into production, which is a
standing audit/compliance exposure and a head start for an attacker who
reads the same advisories. This epic exists to close all four findings; it
does not redesign or re-platform any of the three services.

## Evidence (required)

either (a) a copy of the actual scanned artifact/SBOM showing which
manifest it read, or (b) confirmation of how/where the worker image is
built, since that is not visible in any checked-out repo.

## Hypothesis (required)

We believe bumping the four flagged packages/images to their fixed versions
(storefront: `express` to a version that pins `path-to-regexp>=0.1.12`, and
the Alpine base image to one shipping `libssl3>=3.3.3-r0`; orders:
`golang.org/x/net` to `v0.36.0`; worker: triaging and, if still exposed,
`requests` to `>=2.32.4`) will close all four open scan findings for
storefront, orders, and worker, measured by a rescan reporting 0 open
findings for these four CVEs within 2 weeks of merge, without regressing
each service's existing test suite or its production error rate during
rollout.

## Business goal alignment

Unpatched, publicly-tracked CVEs in production are a standing compliance
and audit risk, and widen the window an opportunistic attacker has once an
advisory is public — `path-to-regexp` and `x/net` both have known
ReDoS/request-smuggling-class advisories in this range. This also protects
the memo's existing north star ([[pmanager-memo]] §2: releases without
customer-facing errors) by routing each fix through the service's normal
test/rollout path rather than a hotfix shortcut.

Fix each of the four findings at its narrowest point (a dependency bump or
a base-image bump) rather than a wider upgrade, to minimize behavior risk
and review surface. The alternative considered — a general "upgrade
everything" pass per repo — was rejected: it would mix unrelated changes
into a security fix, make the scan re-run harder to interpret, and isn't
what the security team flagged. Because storefront and orders each publish
an image that is rolled out from a *different* place than the fix itself
(storefront's rollout lives in the `argocd` repo; orders rolls out its own
Helm chart), fix and rollout are split into separate tasks per service so
each can be reviewed and merged by its owning team without blocking on the
other. Worker has no discoverable deploy/release mechanism in any tracked
repo, so its task only covers the dependency floor; closing the loop on
